title: Infrastructure Telemetry Consumer Registry & Ownership Matrix
author: Jasper Lin
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the canonical registry for consumers of infrastructure telemetry at Redwood Inference, the ownership matrix for telemetry producers and consumers, and the processes to register, change, or retire telemetry contracts. The goal is to reduce alert fatigue, prevent duplicate dashboards, and ensure clear oncall responsibilities for metrics, logs, and traces.

Scope
- Applies to all infrastructure and platform teams that produce or consume platform-level telemetry (metrics, logs, traces, events).
- Consumer types covered: dashboards, alerting rules, SLO reports, cost dashboards, and ML service profiling jobs.
- Out of scope: application-specific business metrics owned by product teams (see related product metrics governance).

Why this matters
- Prevents drift: multiple teams building different dashboards for the same signal without shared context.
- Ensures ownership: clear pager/responsibility for alerts tied to infra signals.
- Improves signal hygiene: standard labels and contracts reduce false positives.

Registry design & schema
The registry is a lightweight catalog stored in Git (infra/telemetry-registry/) and mirrored to the internal Confluence index. Each entry follows the schema below. Entries are YAML files; the registry index in Confluence is a human-readable view of that catalog.

Registry entry (YAML) example (for reference):

---
name: gpu-pool-utilization
signal_type: metric
producer_service: gpu-pool-manager
primary_owner: infra-gpu-team
secondary_owner: serving-runtime
consumer_examples: [cost-dashboard, autoscaler, oncall-alert]
label_contract: ['env', 'region', 'pool_id', 'job_type']
ingestion_tier: core
alertable: true
alert_owners: [infra-gpu-oncall]
retention_policy: 90d
change_window: business-hours
notes: "Primary metric for capacity and autoscaling decisions."
---

Registry fields (human-readable):
- name: short identifier for the signal (snake_case).
- signal_type: metric | log | trace | event.
- producer_service: canonical service name that emits the signal.
- primary_owner / secondary_owner: team names for operational ownership.
- consumer_examples: common consumers to aid impact analysis.
- label_contract: required labels/tags and their semantics.
- ingestion_tier: core | recommended | experimental (impacts retention & SLA).
- alertable: whether alerts should be permitted directly against this signal.
- alert_owners: oncall group(s) to page; must match SRE oncall rosters.
- retention_policy: default retention.
- change_window: preferred times for breaking changes.
- notes: free-form guidance.

Consumer tiers and guidance
- Tier 0 (core): signals required for cluster health, capacity, billing accuracy. Producers must maintain labeling and a 90-day retention. Alertable by default; any alert must be routed to primary owner.
- Tier 1 (recommended): useful operational signals; 30–90 day retention; preferred to be consumed via shared dashboards rather than custom copies.
- Tier 2 (experimental): short-term signals for feature work; 7–30 day retention; no alerts without explicit approval from producer.

Onboarding process (step-by-step)
1. Developer creates a registry YAML in infra/telemetry-registry/{signal-name}.yaml with required fields.
2. Open a Git PR: include sample queries (PromQL/SQL) and an example dashboard panel.
3. Change owner(s) add reviewer(s) from producer and consumer teams.
4. CI checks run: label contract verification, required retention and tier rules.
5. After approvals, merge; the Confluence index auto-updates within 10 minutes.
6. Notify on Slack channel #telemetry-registry with a link to the PR and the dashboard example.

CLI shortcuts (examples)
- Create stub entry: infra-tool telemetry init --name gpu-pool-utilization --type metric --producer gpu-pool-manager
- Validate entry: infra-tool telemetry validate path/to/file.yaml
- List conflicts: infra-tool telemetry conflicts --signal gpu-pool-utilization

Telemetry contracts and backward-compatibility rules
- Producers must not remove required labels without a deprecation notice in the registry and a 2-week migration window.
- Remove or rename metrics only after: (a) registry update, (b) consumers notified, (c) migration runbook published, (d) 2-week wait period unless emergency.
- If a metric changes type (gauge -> counter) the producer must create a new metric name and mark the old one deprecated.

Alerting and dashboard standards
- Naming convention for alerts: svc.signal.short_description (e.g., gpu-pool-manager.utilization.high).
- Alert severity mapping: Sev1 (page) = P99 latency > 2x target OR sustained GPU pool failure of >2 regions; Sev2 (email + Slack) = transient capacity degradation; Sev3 (ticket) = minor deviation with auto-retry.
- Dashboard panel conventions: title = "{service} — {signal} — {operation}", panel description includes link to registry entry, producer owner, and example query.
- Rate limit alerts per signal: maximum of 3 unique pager rules per core signal. If more are needed, consolidate.

Ownership matrix (human-readable table)
| Signal / Service | Primary team | Secondary team | Pager group | Notes |
|------------------|--------------|----------------|-------------|-------|
| gpu-pool-utilization | infra-gpu-team | serving-runtime | infra-gpu-oncall | affects autoscaler and cost dashboards |
| runtime.latency.p99 | serving-runtime | infra-sre | runtime-oncall | High business impact; linked to SLA dashboards |
| storage.iops.threshold | infra-storage | data-platform | infra-storage-oncall | Pager only for sustained degradation > 5m |

Runbook for breaking changes (producer responsibilities)
- Prepare a migration playbook: include queries for identifying consumers, recommended client changes, and rollback steps.
- Coordinate: schedule change during the registry change_window and post to #deployments and #telemetry-registry.
- Run synthetic checks: after change, run 15-minute synthetic checks for core signals to verify no regressions.
- Rollback plan: documented command(s) and expected RTO.

Incident playbook (consumer-facing guidance)
1. Verify the signal: validate queries and labels match registry contract.
2. Escalate: if the pager group matches the registry, follow their oncall steps; otherwise, notify producer primary and open an incident.
3. Short-term mitigations: add temporary dedup or mute rules (documented and timeboxed).
4. Post-incident: add lessons to the registry notes and, if needed, propose schema/label changes via a PR.

Enforcement and CI checks
- The telemetry CI validates: label_contract present, ingestion_tier used correctly, retention defined, and alertable flag consistency.
- PRs that change label_contract require signoff from both primary and secondary owners.

Dashboards & alert hygiene library
- We maintain a panel library (grafana/panels/shared) with vetted visualizations for common signal types. Consumers should prefer building dashboards from library panels rather than ad-hoc panels.
- Shared dashboard ownership: dashboards derived from core signals should include the producer team as watcher and have a documented owner in the dashboard metadata.

Migration & roadmap (next 12 months)
- Q1 2025: complete registry seeding for all core infra signals and run a cross-team audit.
- Q3 2025: enforce CI gate preventing alerts on unregistered signals.
- Q4 2025: build a lightweight UI for telemetry dependency graphs (visualize producers -> consumers).
- 2026: integrate registry with incident automation to auto-open tickets for unregistered consumers.

Operational ownership & contacts
- Registry maintainer: infra-tooling (oncall rota) — infra-tooling@redwood.example.com
- Governance board: Platform Observability Guild: Aisha Kapoor, Miguel Santos, Claire Bennett (rotating chair).

Appendices
A. Example PromQL snippets used in PRs:
- GPU utilization (99th percentile over 5m):
  max_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[5m])
- Node CPU saturation (per region):
  sum(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!='idle'}[5m])) by (region) / sum(machine_cpu_cores) by (region)

B. Dashboard metadata template (JSON) to include in PR:
{
  "title": "{service} - {signal} - example panel",
  "query": "<insert PromQL>",
  "registry_link": "<link>",
  "owner": "team-name"
}

C. Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who can create registry entries?
  A: Any engineer; entries require at least the producer team member as reviewer before merge.
- Q: What if a consumer needs a modified label?
  A: File a PR to adjust the label_contract. Producers must approve; changes follow the standard window.

D. Related policies and runbooks
- Metric deprecation policy (link in repo).
- Oncall escalation playbook (see eng-platform/oncall-and-incident-response).

E. Change log (summary)
- 2024-09-15: Initial draft and registry schema published.
- 2025-06-03: Added ingestion_tier and experimental retention guidance.
- 2026-01-10: Introduced CLI examples and enforcement roadmap.

If you have questions or want to propose a bulk migration of signals, please open a PR against infra/telemetry-registry and ping #telemetry-registry.
